fiction_notice: Original fiction. Not a real event, person, company or recording.

hooks.text: Two hundred thousand messages. Every one of them his.
hooks.note: Good volume shock, but the impossibility is only implied.

hooks.text: He boots the old computer. The conversation never stopped.
hooks.note: Nine words, cause and impossibility together, no technical knowledge needed.

hooks.text: The machine has been in a drawer since 2001. It is still logged in.
hooks.note: Strong, but too long to land inside the first two seconds.

hook_rationale: Hook 2 puts an ordinary action and an impossible result in the same breath, and the word 'stopped' implies a duration the viewer immediately wants measured. Hook 3 says the same thing with five more words, which is five words too many at second zero.
final_twist: The chatroom is not an old conversation still running. It is the live one, and everything the man has said online for twenty-five years has been a delayed copy of it.
music_mood: A single warm analogue drone that sounds like hardware rather than music, sitting just under the CRT hum. It drops out entirely at 0:31 and does not return, so the last sixteen seconds run on room tone and cursor clicks.
sound_bed: CRT degauss, fan hum, mechanical keyboard, and a deliberate three-second delay applied to every modern sound in the final shots.

description: Original fiction - not a real event. Two hundred thousand messages, all in his own handwriting, all saying things he had not thought of yet. Part of an original digital-mystery series.
